newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up sharply, supply woes persist.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up sharply, supply woes persist.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures vaulted to a sharply higher close on Thursday, bolstered by an afternoon round of speculative buying, positive technical indicators and ongoing supply worries, traders said.
Most-active July rose 4.80 cents a lb on the day, to 198.20, having traded from 185.50 to 196.00. Spot May gained 3.10, to finish at 214.30, while the outer months gained between 0.05 and 5.00.
The nearby May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, widened to 21.55 today from 20.90 at the close on Wednesday.
"We have a rather tight situation," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt. "And tightness in deliveries is being exacerbated by the Colombian situation."

The latest bout of supply jitters emerged after a leading coffee official in Colombia said Thursday afternoon that a strike by the country's main trucker drivers' union could delay exports of up to 200,000 70-kg bags of coffee this week and may cause serious problems meeting May export commitments.

"There's an important quantity of coffee that's being held up," Diego Arango Mora, a member of the National Coffee Growers' Committee, told Reuters. "Over the course of this week, the build-up could easily be to the order of 100,000 to 200,000 bags."

A nationwide strike by the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) began at midnight on Saturday. With arabica inventories already near historically low levels in the U.S., traders said a prolonged work stoppage in Colombia, the world's number-two grower, could drive futures prices to new highs.

Earlier in the session, however, market sentiment was dampened by news the Colombian government ordered truckers to end the five-day truckers' strike and said the work stoppage would be declared illegal unless it was called off by midnight.
But union officials brushed aside the government threat, saying that as private citizens they had no obligation to provide any services to the state.
Technically, traders were encouraged by July's finish above Wednesday's high of 196.00 and said the market could test 199.00, a contract high set on Monday, in the near-term.
After Thursday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 6,250 60-kg bags, to 50,350 bags as of April 23. There were 815 bags of coffee pending certification, the exchange said.
The day's volume was estimated at 10,174 lots.
